course_description:
HMST3001 is a work integrated learning course within the Exercise and Sport Sciences and Clinical Exercise Physiology programs. Students complete a semester-long supervised placement experience in an apparently healthy populations setting, applying foundational exercise and sport science knowledge in an authentic workplace environment.

This course is designed to support students to develop professional capability, workplace readiness, communication skills, and reflective practice while contributing meaningfully to the activities of their host organisation. The placement also supports students to meet the relevant apparently healthy population practicum requirements associated with Accredited Exercise Scientist accreditation.

To undertake practicum, students must meet all mandatory requirements as outlined here: Prepare for your Clinical Exercise Physiology placement or Prepare for your Exercise and Sports Sciences placement . Students will also be required to meet any provider specific requirements.

course_aims: Provide students the opportunity to accrue required work experience; apply their knowledge and understanding of the principals of exercise science as they relate to apparently healthy individuals,ﾠand develop professional skills to a standard sufficient to graduate from the program as Accredited Exercise Scientists.

learning_outcomes.description: Interact effectively with other exercise professionals and demonstrate effective written and oral communication skills relevant to the profession
Contribute to the efficient operation of a community, private or government based health and fitness setting or athlete performance environment
Interpret health and fitness assessments, and offer creative solutions to achieve clients' health and fitness goals

Demonstrate the ability to use research skills to critically evaluate specific areas of assessment, client centred interventions and/or education to determine whether research evidence indicates that current practice should be maintained or modified
Develop scientific rationale for professional decision making and service delivery; appropriate time management; and ability to work collaboratively, and independently (as appropriate)
Demonstrate professional conduct that is sensitive to client diversity and equity, and is consistent with the ESSA Code of Professional Conduct and Ethical Practice

assessment_details.title: Initial Logbook Submission
assessment_details.due_date: 5:00 pm on the Friday of your third week of placement.
assessment_details.task_description: To meet ESSA Practicum Standards during your placement, a logbook must be kept detailing all relevant practicum hours. A minimum of 140 hours of practicum is required across a range of exercise science activities to demonstrate competency in assessment, prescription, and delivery within the Accredited Exercise Scientist (AES) scope of practice. Practicum hours must be completed with at least 80 hours assessment, prescription and delivery. The 80 hours are not required to be evenly split across assessment, prescription, and delivery activities. Additionally, up to 60 hours undertaking any other activities that reflect the AES scope of practice. Read full task description Hide full task description
